text:
Martin Necas has 7 goals on 4.4 expected, shooting 19.4%, and the flag on his page says that won't last. The wrinkle: he shot 18% last season too. At some point a hot streak becomes a skill, and our gut says two seasons in, he's closer to that line than our cautious range (centred on 15.9%) admits.

The rest of the game makes his case. He's among the league's fastest (92nd percentile top speed) with a 96th-percentile top shot, and Colorado takes 56.3% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 11th among 401 forwards at 3.4 wins above replacement, with the note that 99th-percentile teammates flatter his raw numbers.

Lately it's 12 points in ten games, 9 of them assists, on ice time down 1:43 a night. And when Artyom Levshunov hit Cale Makar high, the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal wrote that "Martin Necas (Yes, Martin Necas) comes to his defense." Our projection: 77 to 105 points.
headline: Necas keeps finishing like it's a skill
